; Bank0OpeningSequence — physical $00010..$001A1 (exclusive).
; One-shot scene setup consumes scene_init_pending, seeds coordinates/countdowns and queues a
; 23-byte VRAM command. The update path advances a scroll-delta sequence and timed palette
; changes; final input selects a scene transition. The characters and exact sequence meanings
; remain uncertain.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $0004C. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Per-frame entry: initialize once, advance scroll and actors, clear/draw OAM, then test the
; requested scene transition.
; A is the requested next-scene identifier. Clear the trigger event and publish the completion
; sentinel.
; Alternate setup clears the scroll, palette and cursor flags, reloads the scene palette and resumes
; the common scroll initializer with Y=$EC. A normal selecting caller is unresolved.
; Alternate two palettes only on animation frame $0B while the result gate is clear; consume
; the scroll delay afterward.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $00171, $00137. Repeated
; values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Bank0OpeningAnimation — physical $001A1..$0046B (exclusive).
; Toggle the frame parity, dispatch through local_phase, and update the second moving object.
; Timed frame sequences use parallel delay/frame tables; later phases request a CHR change.
; Nine inline tail targets select the local animation phases; their bank context is the opening pair.
; Little-endian CPU targets for the immediately preceding stack-pop dispatcher. The caller does not
; return into these words; selectors and the scene bank pair govern the chosen entry.
; Four little-endian CPU pointers to eight-byte VRAM commands, selected by the opening text state.
; Four eight-byte commands copied by the opening text helper; each includes its queue
; control/address/payload bytes.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $00257. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Count down each frame duration. Frames 11 and 12 enable motion/audio and restore the palette; frame
; 14 advances phase, changes CHR and separates the two X positions. The ADC carry deliberately flows
; into the following SBC.
; Repeat frames 14..19, then place the extra object beside the left actor and start its motion cursor
; and sound.
; Repeat frames 20..25 while moving the two main X positions inward by two pixels; the final
; repetition starts the next timed phase.
; After the wait, request the next CHR page and palette and start a two-frame timed loop with audio.
; Repeat the late two-frame sequence while lowering the third Y field toward its stopping thresholds.
; Then queue a twelve-byte VRAM fragment and begin frames 4..6.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $003E9. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Repeat frames 4..6, then frames 2..3 while scroll completion is set. The final path resets
; phase/frame delay and requests the next scene bank.
; Bank0DeltaMotion — physical $0046B..$005AC (exclusive).
; Accumulate paired coordinate deltas from a word-stride sequence. A second byte of $80 ends
; motion, disables this object and enables its successor; alternating frames advance the
; cursor and a separate countdown controls mirroring.
; Successive (X delta,Y delta) bytes added to the opening object position. A second-byte $80 at pair
; 112 terminates the 226-byte stream.
; Bank0OpeningSprites — physical $005AC..$014D8 (exclusive).
; Rebuild OAM in a phase-dependent order. Two objects use mirrored frame ranges; the extra
; object has its own position and horizontal-flip flag. Alternating drawing order reduces
; persistent sprite priority. Unclassified tables and intervening bytes retain their original
; representation.
; Start OAM at the sentinel cursor $FF. Phase chooses which actor groups exist and their
; drawing order.
; Draw the current animation frame plus $34 at fixed X=100 and the animated third Y coordinate, behind
; background tiles.
; Phase 8 draws a fixed emblem; the palette-animation flag separately enables a frame selected by the
; palette cursor at fixed screen coordinates.
; Tail-call the shared metasprite emitter with frame $3C at (80,64).
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $002E0, $00462, $00030,
; $00234. Repeated values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping
; and any unobserved selection remain unresolved.
; Packed tile indices in sixteen-byte blocks, read as four rows of four tiles by the nametable
; builder. This region can contain multiple adjacent blocks; scene-selected bank/pointer context
; determines the base.
; Sixty-four nametable attribute bytes, copied by the scene-selected attribute pointer. Each byte
; packs four two-bit palette selections.
; 240 bytes indexed by the opening scroll cursor. Each sample changes the scroll and the cursor resets
; at $F0; the following pointer table is separate.
; Little-endian CPU pointers to count-prefixed metasprites in this scene bank. Table aliases may
; overlap; this physical batch does not claim that every selector is naturally reached.
; Adjacent metasprite records: one sprite count followed by count four-byte (Y
; offset,tile,attributes,X offset) entries. The shared emitter adds the sprite origin, applies
; mirror/attribute rules and writes OAM. Boundaries follow the individual counts; this incbin may
; include several records.
; Seven adjacent four-byte sprite-like groups have fixed Y/attribute fields and stepped X. Nearby
; count-prefixed sprite consumers were checked; a separate header and selecting index for these groups
; remain unresolved.
; Adjacent metasprite records: one sprite count followed by count four-byte (Y
; offset,tile,attributes,X offset) entries. The shared emitter adds the sprite origin, applies
; mirror/attribute rules and writes OAM. Boundaries follow the individual counts; this incbin may
; include several records.
; ModeSelection — physical $014D8..$01910 (exclusive).
; Initialize mode-selection RAM, then accept Start or a selected target to commit the choice.
; Select cycles four options with a release latch. Menu text is assembled from length-prefixed
; fragments into the VRAM command queue; palette rotation animates the pending selection. An
; inactivity counter eventually requests a transition.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $01556. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; A/X supply source low/high bytes. Prefix byte is payload length; queue_write_index is
; advanced by the copied byte count.
; Selector bytes, ROM-word runs and repeated attribute-fill values lie between code and metasprite
; records. Neighboring consumers were inspected; the exact division into original tables remains
; unresolved.
; Trigger-evaluation handler for scene 8 sets the shot counter to $FF. The same CPU alias under other
; scene banks is not this physical routine.
; Packed tile indices in sixteen-byte blocks, read as four rows of four tiles by the nametable
; builder. This region can contain multiple adjacent blocks; scene-selected bank/pointer context
; determines the base.
; Uniform $FF bytes between independently bounded structures. Original fill purpose is unresolved.
; Sixty-four nametable attribute bytes, copied by the scene-selected attribute pointer. Each byte
; packs four two-bit palette selections.
; Bank0GallerySetup — physical $01910..$01C09 (exclusive).
; Initialize parallel object arrays and round-dependent parameters. The introductory state
; machine moves an object to Y=$6A, cycles its frames and returns it to Y=$80. Round is
; advanced with a cap of 99; a timed toggle switches a requested CHR bank. Exact gallery
; identity is not assigned solely from these mechanics.
; Initialize the indexed arrays for active_object_count slots; mode and round choose
; counts/timers independently of natural reachability.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $01931, $01937, $01962.
; Repeated values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any
; unobserved selection remain unresolved.
; Clear the selection, start the indexed effect/frame delay and account for remaining targets once.
; Special targets update mode-dependent counts and audio; ordinary targets start a score event and
; scan nearby objects.
; Compare object coordinates against the selected object using the actual carry chain, requiring each
; reduced difference below eight. Eligible neighbors enter the hit/hidden state and get a ten-point
; request; the loop ends at active_object_count.
; Every 32 service ticks, toggle the requested CHR1 value between $1D and $09. This is a
; mapper request, not a physical bank number.
; Little-endian CPU targets for the immediately preceding stack-pop dispatcher. The caller does not
; return into these words; selectors and the scene bank pair govern the chosen entry.
; Clear the batch flag and request result music only when its latch differs. Wait for all objects to
; reach state 2, then restart a batch or select the result animation from mode and remaining-target
; state.
; Advance the selected result frame range on its delay, move the intro actor toward its Y thresholds
; and award the threshold score. Once the final frame/wait finishes, set scene_result or
; scene_completion_flag according to remaining targets.
; Repeated delay/coordinate parameters follow the phase routines. Reload consumers and adjacent
; boundaries were inspected; individual subtable grouping remains unresolved.
; Bank0ObjectUpdate — physical $01C09..$01EA4 (exclusive).
; During local phase 4, service each indexed object. Delays gate movement; out-of-range
; coordinates trigger reset/remaining-target handling. Frame and motion sequences are indirect
; ROM lookups with state-dependent alternatives; recovered continuations describe the same indexed arrays.
; Clear the per-object accounted flag and reduce the batch parameter. The reset path parks an inactive
; object at ($80,$E0); the active path randomizes spawn position and motion parameters.
; Split one RNG byte into spawn, direction, palette and motion selectors. Optional effects depend on
; mode, round and other effect slots; initialize frame and packed-motion cursors before returning.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $01C91, $01C97. Repeated
; values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Optionally negate the horizontal delta, save it and add it to X. Select a packed signed vertical
; pattern, decode its current sample and subtract it from Y; advance the sample cursor until $C0.
; Repeated small movement/animation values form non-code data between bounded neighbors. Their exact
; grouping and game meaning remain unresolved.
; A complete ROM-pointer prefix leads into repeated small parameter records. Neighboring frame
; consumers were checked; no complete original record schema is asserted.
; Effect targets use a special frame in one play mode; otherwise a delay bit chooses between adjacent
; frames. This supplements the common indirect-frame selection path.
; Reset motion/frame/hidden/variant fields, park the object offscreen and mark its remaining-target
; accounting complete.
; Store the new frame cursor and obtain its delay from the shared duration bytes.
; Bank0ObjectSprites — physical $01EA4..$02C0C (exclusive).
; Build OAM from parallel position/frame/state arrays. An alternating parity pass changes
; drawing order; clipping and object state select priority and palette overrides. Animated
; effects have separate countdowns and frame bases. Outside the active phase, draw the
; introductory object and its associated overlay.
; Y selects the object. Compute frame/attributes and clipping before the shared OAM emitter;
; caller-supplied offsets support effect sprites.
; Select an effect delta, add it to the object's Y and update the packed-motion cursor. A terminal
; sample clears the effect and parks the object offscreen.
; Resolve the frame variant from intro Y, batch-reset state, play mode and remaining targets before
; joining the common drawing path.
; Sprite/tile parameters and repeated $FF/$0F/$00 bit patterns precede the supported tile records.
; Specific original grouping is unresolved.
; Reset the OAM cursor, convert the one-based candidate index to Y, reject ineligible object
; phases/states and draw its effect or normal test sprite. Selection mechanics do not establish a
; natural Zapper hit in the current emulator.
; Tile-pattern bytes contain repeated nibble/plane motifs between supported block data and the next
; pointer table. No unsupported consumed-block domain is claimed.
; Little-endian CPU pointers to count-prefixed metasprites in this scene bank. Table aliases may
; overlap; this physical batch does not claim that every selector is naturally reached.
; Scene 3 element 35 points to the generic zero byte at $02A21; its presence does not prove
; a valid empty record or a naturally selected frame.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $020BF, $01FC7, $01FD3,
; $01F8D. Repeated values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping
; and any unobserved selection remain unresolved.
; Adjacent metasprite records: one sprite count followed by count four-byte (Y
; offset,tile,attributes,X offset) entries. The shared emitter adds the sprite origin, applies
; mirror/attribute rules and writes OAM. Boundaries follow the individual counts; this incbin may
; include several records.
; Adjacent metasprite records: one sprite count followed by count four-byte (Y
; offset,tile,attributes,X offset) entries. The shared emitter adds the sprite origin, applies
; mirror/attribute rules and writes OAM. Boundaries follow the individual counts; this incbin may
; include several records.
; Generic storage byte $00: scene 3 frame-table element 35 at physical $02436 points here
; (CPU $AA11, effective PRG banks [0,1,6,7]). The surrounding count/field grammar closes at
; $02A3C. This does not establish a safe empty sprite: the emitter executes its body before
; decrementing the count, so zero underflows. Natural selection and sentinel meaning remain unknown.
; Adjacent metasprite records: one sprite count followed by count four-byte (Y
; offset,tile,attributes,X offset) entries. The shared emitter adds the sprite origin, applies
; mirror/attribute rules and writes OAM. Boundaries follow the individual counts; this incbin may
; include several records.
; Packed tile indices in sixteen-byte blocks, read as four rows of four tiles by the nametable
; builder. This region can contain multiple adjacent blocks; scene-selected bank/pointer context
; determines the base.
; Sixty-four nametable attribute bytes, copied by the scene-selected attribute pointer. Each byte
; packs four two-bit palette selections.
; Bank1GallerySequence — physical $02C0C..$02EAC (exclusive).
; One-shot initialization derives palette, object count and timing from mode and round. The
; local-phase dispatcher runs an introductory object across the screen, cycles delay tables
; and switches into active play. It updates round up to 99 and tracks whether the object batch
; completed successfully.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $02C5D. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Mark the selected object hit/accounted, save its coordinates and motion direction, then choose
; special-target score/count handling. Ordinary targets derive their score bucket by dividing the
; saved Y coordinate by 32.
; Little-endian CPU targets for the immediately preceding stack-pop dispatcher. The caller does not
; return into these words; selectors and the scene bank pair govern the chosen entry.
; Advance phase and animation frame, load the indexed duration and request CHR page $10.
; On timeout choose scene completion when no targets remain, otherwise the negative scene-result path.
; A paired state test awards fifty points and selects music; later frame gates start the next intro or
; restart a batch.
; Reset frame/CHR, choose three intro repetitions and reload the first duration. Object iteration and
; initial-delay expiry prepare the palette and next initialization according to play mode.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $02D83, $02DA0, $02E13,
; $02DF7. Repeated values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping
; and any unobserved selection remain unresolved.
; Bank1ObjectUpdate — physical $02EAC..$0302E (exclusive).
; Service each active slot: countdown, boundary handling, random respawn and parallel
; movement/frame sequences. Respawns choose a masked random position/type and reset the
; sequence cursors. Mode and remaining-target fields affect the next batch; state 2 is handled
; separately from moving targets.
; X selects the object. Respawn waits for its delay, checks both screen bounds, then resets
; motion/frame cursors from random bits.
; Park the object at X=0,Y=8 when the shared update path retires it.
; Carry and mode parameters gate an optional type-bit restriction. The alternate state setter marks
; the object accounted and rejoins the shared state assignment; a selecting caller remains unresolved.
; Fetch the indexed horizontal magnitude, invert it according to the saved direction flag, add it with
; the existing carry and advance the motion cursor until its table endpoint.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $02FBC, $02FA9, $02F2B.
; Repeated values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any
; unobserved selection remain unresolved.
; X selects the object. Parallel frame and duration streams use the same cursor; object state
; chooses the alternate half of a stream.
; Bank1ObjectSprites — physical $0302E..$031A9 (exclusive).
; Draw targets with per-object clipping, palette overrides and alternating frame priority.
; During non-active phases render the introductory sprite and status overlay. Sprite positions
; come from separate indexed X/Y arrays; tile-frame bases are ROM tables, whose complete
; structure is not classified here.
; Decrement the effect lifetime, choose a normal score frame or mode-specific effect frame, move its
; saved Y upward and emit at the saved X.
; Convert the candidate index, reject nonzero object state and otherwise draw the background test
; frame with priority bit $20.
; Repeated delay/frame runs, pointer arrays and tile motifs lie beside the gallery-1 motion/frame
; consumers. The interval is non-code; complete subtable grouping remains unresolved.
; Repeated movement/frame bytes and independently supported metasprite pointer bytes. Scene 5 replaces
; default grid 5, so these bytes do not establish consumed 4x4 tile blocks; shared/overlapping roles
; are retained only where independently supported.
; Little-endian CPU pointers to count-prefixed metasprites in this scene bank. Table aliases may
; overlap; this physical batch does not claim that every selector is naturally reached.
; Adjacent metasprite records: one sprite count followed by count four-byte (Y
; offset,tile,attributes,X offset) entries. The shared emitter adds the sprite origin, applies
; mirror/attribute rules and writes OAM. Boundaries follow the individual counts; this incbin may
; include several records.
; Packed tile indices in sixteen-byte blocks, read as four rows of four tiles by the nametable
; builder. This region can contain multiple adjacent blocks; scene-selected bank/pointer context
; determines the base.
; Sixty-four nametable attribute bytes, copied by the scene-selected attribute pointer. Each byte
; packs four two-bit palette selections.
; Uniform $FF bytes between independently checked boundaries. Non-code classification is established;
; original fill/alignment intent remains unresolved.
; Bank2GalleryFrame — physical $04010..$04198 (exclusive).
; Consume scene initialization, seed two animated actors, then run per-frame animation,
; timers, target handling, OAM and shared scene-transition checks. Paired counters and state
; flags coordinate two independent objects; no complete game-level interpretation is claimed
; for every flag.
; Unknown singleton at physical $0403A: byte $00. The isolated BRK/RTS shape and adjacent structures
; do not discriminate an entry from inert data. Retain the exact byte without code/data inference; see
; uncertainties.md.
; A two-byte result delay gates the result animation. Once active, a six-tick cadence selects
; VRAM fragments and eventually requests scene completion.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $0413E, $04148. Repeated
; values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; A separate overlay cursor uses the same six-tick cadence; $F0 disables it after five
; entries.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $0417C, $04186. Repeated
; values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Bank2ActorEntry — physical $04198..$042C1 (exclusive).
; Dispatch by the gallery phase. Entry motion waits on a delay, adjusts coordinates and
; initializes both animation channels when the threshold is reached. A second coordinate
; counter removes priority during the entry.
; Little-endian CPU targets for the immediately preceding stack-pop dispatcher. The caller does not
; return into these words; selectors and the scene bank pair govern the chosen entry.
; Unknown singleton at physical $041AC: byte $60. The isolated BRK/RTS shape and adjacent structures
; do not discriminate an entry from inert data. Retain the exact byte without code/data inference; see
; uncertainties.md.
; After the batch wait, seed two sequences, entry delays, cursors and starting Y positions, select CHR
; 6 and advance the gallery phase.
; Countdown thresholds queue result fragments and adjust actor sequences. On rollover increment round
; with a cap of 99, clear selected/extra state and restart the random-parameter initializer.
; Bank2ActorTriggers — physical $042C1..$043D5 (exclusive).
; Advance the entry phase after a 96-tick timer. Two separate animation-frame tests spawn the
; corresponding secondary object at an offset from each actor; active/result flags suppress
; repeated triggers.
; Unknown singleton at physical $042E8: byte $60. The isolated BRK/RTS shape and adjacent structures
; do not discriminate an entry from inert data. Retain the exact byte without code/data inference; see
; uncertainties.md.
; When the secondary object is inactive, reduce the position parameter and randomize the next entry
; wait. On the exact terminal frame/delay pair, choose the follow-up sequence and reset its cursor.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $04326. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Mirror the entry-delay/sequence transition for the second actor, using its own terminal frame and
; duration table.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $04393. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Return a uniformly masked RNG index 0..3 in Y for entry-delay tables; A also contains the masked
; value.
; Bank2SecondaryAnimation — physical $043D5..$044CF (exclusive).
; Initialize and service the two secondary objects symmetrically. Each object copies animation
; identifier, delay and cursor into the shared sequencer and receives its next frame.
; Each result path checks its own frame/boundary conditions before recycling the object.
; First secondary-object setup; its result flag and the selection variant determine the helper
; path before animation state is loaded.
; Save the shared sequencer's cursor, frame and delay, draw the first secondary object and check its
; result/boundary state.
; Transfer position, attributes, mirror and frame into shared sprite scratch and tail-call the
; metasprite emitter.
; Second secondary-object setup mirrors the first using the second actor record and X=1 helper
; contract.
; Save the second sequencer result, draw it and run its result/boundary checks with X=1.
; Transfer the second secondary object's sprite fields into shared scratch and emit its metasprite.
; Offset a secondary object from the extra actor's position using its direction index; choose the
; destination attribute field from X.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $044AF. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Bank2ActorSprites — physical $044CF..$04687 (exclusive).
; Emit the two secondary sprites only when their active/result gates allow it. Main actors run
; animation before metasprite emission; frame-match tables optionally add overlays or queue
; VRAM updates. A parity toggle alternates which group is drawn first.
; Compare the current second-actor frame against five keys. Queue a VRAM fragment only when
; the matched key differs from the cached key.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $0457C, $04592. Repeated
; values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $045D1, $045E9. Repeated
; values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $04601, $04619. Repeated
; values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; A completed result waits for terminal animation frames before randomization. Otherwise screen-edge
; checks start a disappearance sequence or reset the actor; successful departure increments selected-
; target count and saturates remaining targets at zero.
; Bank2ActorRandomization — physical $04687..$04767 (exclusive).
; Load an eight-byte interleaved parameter record selected by difficulty, then use masked
; pseudo-random bits to select actor parameters. Separate setup paths initialize each actor
; and advance the gallery phase. Round-dependent gates restrict the low-bit record selector
; before loading the next interleaved parameter set.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $0468A, $0468F. Repeated
; values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Apply the corresponding frame, boundary and disappearance transitions to the second secondary
; object, with the same guarded target accounting.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $0470F, $04714, $04719.
; Repeated values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any
; unobserved selection remain unresolved.
; Restrict the random selector to the supported range, fold selector 3 to zero and use twice the
; remaining selector plus a per-actor base to load an interleaved parameter record.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $0475F. Repeated values
; and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping and any unobserved
; selection remain unresolved.
; Bank2BatchCompletion — physical $04767..$048E1 (exclusive).
; Draw timed result effects, then wait until both effects and the phase timer finish.
; Remaining targets, mode and batch-result fields decide whether to continue, award a 50-unit
; score event or begin a result animation. The next batch resets shared actor/secondary-object
; state.
; Result mode selects sequence $2A, fixed frame $48 and entry delay before resetting phase/batch
; state. The update also redraws the main actors and counts down difficulty parameters before setting
; the result-mode flag.
; Bank2DifficultyAndResult — physical $048E1..$0499A (exclusive).
; Compute max(0, 5 - (randomized parameter + difficulty)). At the result threshold choose
; actor animation scripts from success flags and mode; set a timer, palette and optional VRAM
; update. Exact meaning of each result flag remains tentative.
; Select CHR $15, disable the extra object and redraw the main actors with a reset OAM cursor.
; Unknown singleton at physical $04999: byte $60. Apparent pointer hits are overlapping repeated frame
; bytes; neither those occurrences nor the RTS shape prove entry. Retain the exact byte without
; code/data inference; see uncertainties.md.
; Bank2ParameterRecord — physical $0499A..$04A37 (exclusive).
; A selects an eight-byte ROM record through a pointer table. Copy its bytes to every other
; RAM address starting at $0456+X; this is an interleaved pair of actor parameter records, not
; a contiguous eight-byte destination.
; A is the record selector; X is the destination lane. Interleave eight source bytes at stride
; two, preserving the adjacent actor lane.
; Pointers with an eight-byte stride and repeated signed coordinate/delta fields occur beside the
; actor consumers. Exact record grouping and selection remain unresolved.
; Bank2ActorSequencing — physical $04A37..$04B3B (exclusive).
; Each actor may switch from an idle animation after position comparisons and its own delay
; expire. Shared animation inputs return the next frame, cursor and delay; those outputs are
; copied back to the actor record.
; Draw secondary overlays only when their active flags and main-frame cursors permit. Table-driven
; positions follow the main entry frames; the second overlay temporarily uses background priority.
; ROM parameter bytes inspected against their indexed consumers at physical $04AF3, $04AF9, $04B13,
; $04B19. Repeated values and neighboring code/data bound this interval; original subtable grouping
; and any unobserved selection remain unresolved.
; Bank2HitHandling — physical $04B3B..$04D57 (exclusive).
; Consume a selected target once, decrement remaining targets and update result state. The
; hit-selected object determines the effect and follow-up animation. A threshold lookup
; converts a vertical coordinate into score/effect values. Normal Zapper hit production is
; untested; these are static mechanics.
; Mark the first result, derive the height reward, start its effect animation/timer at the hit
; coordinates and record success. Result mode changes the sequence, count adjustment and audio while
; suppressing the immediate score delta.
